sections.h2: France, the Netherlands and Spain took most of the EU's LNG imports in 2025

chart.title: France took 31 bcm in 2025, more than the Netherlands or Spain
chart.sub: EU LNG imports by Member State, bcm, 2025.

sections.means: France was the largest EU importer in 2025, ahead of the Netherlands at 24 bcm and Spain at 23 bcm.
sections.todo: Track Belgium and Italy, which added the most volume in 2025, against the refill need.

sections.h2: One supplier, the United States, provided 58% of EU LNG imports in 2025

chart.title: The United States sent 84 of the EU's 146 bcm of LNG in 2025

sections.means: ACER reports the United States at 58% of EU LNG imports, roughly a quarter of all EU gas consumption.
sections.todo: Diversify supply before the end of 2026 Russian LNG cutoff, because new capacity only lands in 2029 to 2031.

sections.h2: India's LNG capacity is one terminal running flat out, Dahej at 95%

chart.title: Dahej runs at 95.1%; the next highest, Dabhol, runs at 42.7%
chart.source: PNGRB, NG Demand Projections for 2030 and 2040, section 4.2, citing PPAC.

sections.means: Across all eight terminals India ran at 50.5% in FY2023-24, with Dahej at 95.1% and most others far lower.
sections.todo: Tie new regas capacity to pipelines and demand centres, as PNGRB advises, before adding more terminals.
